chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the son of a paternal half-sister and the son of a maternal half-sister. He said, 'For the son of the maternal sister is one-sixth, and for the son of the paternal sister is the remainder.'

key_terms.ابْنُ أُخْتٍ: Son of a sister (half-sister in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a son of a paternal half-sister versus a son of a maternal half-sister?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the distribution of the residual estate (al-baqi) among specific half-siblings when no primary heirs exist, assigning one-sixth to the son of the paternal half-sister and the remainder to the son of the maternal half-sister. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between paternal and maternal lines in inheritance, where the maternal connection often carries a fixed share while the paternal line may absorb the surplus. It serves as a key example of how the Imams interpreted the general verses of Surah An-Nisa to resolve specific kinship scenarios not explicitly detailed in the Quranic text.
